title: Recognition of normalization without a Noetherian source
statement: Let $T$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $a:Z\to T$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Assume that every local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], that $a$ induces a bijection between the generic points of irreducible components of $Z$ and of $T$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], and that for every such generic point $z$ the induced map $\kappa(a(z))\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there is a unique isomorphism of $T$-schemes $Z\xrightarrow{\sim}T^\nu$, where $T^\nu\to T$ is the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. No local Noetherianity of $Z$, finiteness of $a$, excellence, or reducedness of $T$ is assumed. The empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 035Q, lemma-normalization-normal (3), including its footnote on reductions, and Tag 0H7D, lemma-normalization-trivial; uniqueness from 035Q (4). The generic-point bijection gives finitely many components over each affine open of T, without assuming Z locally Noetherian.

proof.text: Every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq T$ is a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme: open subschemes are locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] to $U$ to obtain finitely many irreducible components. Thus the normalization theorems apply to $T$.

source.place: 035Q, hypothesis on X; verification using Properties 0BA8.

proof.text: For any scheme $S$ and open $V\subseteq S$, the irreducible components of $V$ are exactly $C\cap V$ for components $C$ of $S$ meeting $V$: an open meeting $C$ contains its generic point, and closure in $S$ of a component of $V$ is a maximal irreducible closed subset of $S$. Hence their generic points are exactly the component-generic points of $S$ lying in $V$. Apply this to $U\subseteq T$ and $a^{-1}U\subseteq Z$. The assumed generic-point bijection restricts to a bijection between these two sets. Therefore $a^{-1}U$ has finitely many components for every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq T$. For any quasi-compact open $W\subseteq Z$, cover $W$ by finitely many opens $a^{-1}U_i$ with $U_i$ affine in $T$; each component-generic point of $W$ is a component-generic point of $Z$ in one of these opens. Their union is finite, so $W$ has finitely many components. This proves the required condition on $Z$ without local Noetherianity of $Z$.

source.place: 035Q (3), verification of finiteness of components on inverse images; elementary open-set argument.

proof.text: Domain local rings imply that $Z$ is reduced: a nilpotent section has zero germ at every point and is zero by the sheaf axiom. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme], $a$ factors through $T_{\mathrm{red}}$. Reduction does not change the underlying space or residue fields: affine-locally it is $A\to A/\sqrt{0}$, and quotienting either ring by a prime and taking its fraction field gives the same field. For a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq T$, both $U_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $a^{-1}U$ are reduced. On affine neighborhoods their component-generic stalks are localizations at minimal primes. The field conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] identifies these stalks canonically with their residue fields (the maximal ideals are zero). Under those identifications the generic local-ring maps are exactly the residue-field maps in the hypothesis. They are isomorphisms, and step 2 gives the generic-point bijections. Thus the induced maps on reductions have the required generic-point bijections and generic-local-ring isomorphisms.

source.place: 035Q (3), footnote on reductions; definition-birational; Algebra Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-normalization-integral-birational-factor] to $a:Z	o T$. Step 1 verifies its target condition; step 2 verifies the finite-component condition on all inverse images; step 3 verifies its reduced generic local-ring condition. It gives $e:T^
u\xrightarrow{\sim}Z^
u$ with $a\circ
u_Z\circ e=
u_T$. This use of 035Q (3) does not require $Z$ normal, finite type, or locally Noetherian.

Apply [lem-sfb-normalization-normal-locally-finite] to $Z$, using the given integrally closed domain local rings and the quasi-compact-open finiteness proved in step 2. It makes $
u_Z:Z^
u	o Z$ an isomorphism. Thus $b=
u_Z\circ e:T^
u	o Z$ is an isomorphism, and step 4 gives $a\circ b=
u_T$. Its inverse $b^{-1}:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}T^
u$ satisfies $
u_T\circ b^{-1}=a$, as required.

source.place: 0H7D, normalization of a normal scheme is trivial.

proof.text: Each irreducible component of $Z$ dominates its corresponding component of $T$: its image contains the image of its generic point, which is the target generic point, and continuity places the image in the closure of that point. Apply [lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift] to $a$, with the normality of $Z$ and step 1 for $T$. There is at most one morphism $Z\to T^\nu$ over $T$, so the inverse from step 5 is the unique such isomorphism. If $T$ is empty then any morphism to it has empty source; all constructions above are empty and give the unique isomorphism. No finiteness of $a$, excellence or reducedness of $T$ has been introduced.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_iso_reducedNormalization_of_integral_normal_generic {T Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian T] (a : Z ⟶ T) [IsIntegralHom a] (hZ : ∀ z : Z, IsDomain (Z.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Z.presheaf.stalk z)) (hgeneric : Set.BijOn a {z : Z | ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, IsGenericPoint z C} {t : T | ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents T, IsGenericPoint t C}) (hresidue : ∀ z : Z, (∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, IsGenericPoint z C) → IsIso (a.residueFieldMap z)) : ∃! e : Z ≅ T.reducedNormalization, e.hom ≫ T.fromReducedNormalization = a

reviewed_lean.note: Clause by clause: [IsLocallyNoetherian T], [IsIntegralHom a] (not finite), hZ normal-domain stalks in the recorded inline form, Set.BijOn on component generic points of Z and T, hresidue IsIso (a.residueFieldMap z) at generic z, conclusion ∃! e : Z ≅ T.reducedNormalization with e.hom ≫ fromReducedNormalization = a. This matches the node and Stacks 035Q(3)(4)/0H7D with no stronger hypotheses. Single explicit universe u, as the node and the citer reducedNormalization_smooth_pullback need. Edge cases checked: empty T, empty Z with nonempty T, nonreduced T (k[ε] vs k), infinitely many locally finite components. Node differs from side-live only in lean; lean.statement verbatim in the file; no definitions; proof is sorry only; source and blueprint docstrings and all 6 proof steps present; imports exist.
